findings.text: Nested IO and MSR bitmap controls are vacuous when the corresponding CPU based use bit is clear; when set the configured guest addresses must satisfy the page address validity predicate, otherwise entry is rejected.

TPR shadow checks require a valid virtual APIC page when enabled and require a zero high nibble of threshold when virtual interrupt delivery is off. An extra virtual TPR versus threshold nibble comparison runs only under warning mode, running vCPU, TPR shadow without delivery or APIC access virtualization, and successful VM scoped guest read.

APIC access virtualization requires a valid access page. APIC virtualization features require TPR shadow, forbid combining x2APIC virtualization with APIC access virtualization, require exit on interrupts when delivery is enabled, and for posted interrupts require delivery plus interrupt acknowledge on exit plus constrained notification vector and aligned descriptor address.
Page modification logging is vacuous unless enabled; when enabled it requires EPT and a valid logging address. The enabled predicate reflects the secondary execution PML bit.

Unrestricted guest and mode based EPT execution each require EPT when requested. Shadow VMCS is vacuous unless enabled, otherwise both read and write bitmap addresses must satisfy page address validity.
NMI controls require NMI exiting when virtual NMIs are requested, and require virtual NMIs when NMI window exiting is requested. Virtual NMI state reflects the pin based control bit.

EPTP is accepted only for UC or WB memory types advertised in capabilities, page walk length 4 or 5 as advertised, legal GPA with reserved field clear, and address and dirty enable only if advertised.

VMFUNC enable reflects its secondary control; EPTP switching additionally requires the function control bit. Save preemption timer reflects the exit control bit. Reported CR3 target count derives from the nested misc low value.

Exit controls must verify against allowed low and high masks and both exit MSR load and store lists must pass MSR switch validation. MSR switch accepts zero count, rejects counts above the atomic limit, and otherwise requires aligned base plus legal end address.

Entry controls must verify against allowed masks and the entry MSR load list must validate. Injected event info when valid constrains type, vector, error code presence, reserved bits and instruction length, with protected mode derived from unrestricted guest and CR0 PE and with capability dependent handling of other events, zero length, and hardware error code checks.
Only double fault, task segment, segment not present, stack, general protection, page fault and alignment check vectors are defined as carrying an error code.

Host state validation covers fixed bit valid CR0 and CR4 plus legal CR3, CET write protect dependence, canonical sysenter pointers, conditional PAT and perf control validity, address space size dependent CR4 and RIP and entry mode limits, selector privilege and table bits plus null selector rules, canonical host bases and exit RIP width selected by LA57, and EFER and CET consistency when corresponding loads are requested.
SMI window enable is effectively a no operation because resume from system management is expected to exit anyway; the outer entry point additionally guards against trust domain vCPUs.

Instruction emulation checking for trust domain vCPUs requests instruction retry to support MMIO handling, otherwise it delegates. INIT and SIPI signalling is reported blocked for trust domain vCPUs, otherwise blocked only while VMXON is active outside guest mode.

Virtual APIC mode selection is skipped for trust domain vCPUs and when no in kernel LAPIC or no relevant acceleration exists. XAPIC selects access virtualization with page reload and a mode dependent TLB action; X2APIC selects X2APIC virtualization when supported; masks are then refreshed for X2APIC.

Constructed EPTP uses write back memory type, walk length 4 for dummy roots and otherwise 4 or 5 from root level, plus dirty tracking when globally and per root enabled; a missing backing page yields an invalid value. Flushing uses context sync for a valid page and global sync otherwise, issued through INVEPT with an EPTP plus reserved operand.
Virtual APIC mode update holds the VMCS01 guard while reading and rewriting secondary execution controls.

Virtual TPR consistency cannot be decided once because the guest can rewrite the in memory value after validation, so hardware remains responsible at actual entry; failed guest reads are treated as benign under bus error read semantics, and reads use a VM scoped path and run state gate to avoid SMRAM and unrestored memslot effects.
MSR switch lists require 16 byte alignment and posted interrupt descriptors require 64 byte alignment and legal GPA.
Virtual TPR comparison and host TPR threshold checks use 4 bit nibbles, and posted notification vector reserves its upper byte as zero.
